audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows disagreed with their own whys: row 0 read Skill under a why saying the stage favours Poppy, and rows 4, 5 and 6 read Skill/Poppy/Poppy under whys saying 'favouring you' twice and 'outlasts her'.
audit.why: The packet chart (Poppy / Poppy / Poppy / Skill / Vladimir / Vladimir / Vladimir) matches the prose row for row, and the mirror audit (poppy__vladimir) already flipped rows 5 and 6 to Vladimir for the same reason. Poppy is a peel tank with no ranged pressure and no sustain; a 50.63% lane that she wins early has to end with Vladimir.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 4, 5 and 6 flipped in phases[N].side and win[N] as one paired atomic group.

audit.why: Poppy's spikes are levels 1-3 and her E; Vladimir's are Hemoplague at 6 and his AP items. The spike entries already say so.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text promised you can 'grind her down safely' with chip damage, and dontsFull[1].d carried a generic template body under the title 'Get R-knocked mid-poke'.
audit.why: Steadfast Presence passively grants Poppy Armor and Magic Resist that INCREASE as her health drops — so grinding her low is exactly when your chip stops working, which is the opposite of what the page implies. It also stops enemy dashes around her, then slows and grounds whoever it caught. Heroic Charge is a 475-range dash on 14s at rank 1 that only stuns if it pushes you into a wall, and Keeper's Verdict is a channel that knocks you a very long way — which is what removes you from your own Hemoplague zone.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text now states the low-health resist scaling and turns the advice into forcing a recall; dontsFull[1].d now says what her ult actually does to you.

audit.whatIsWrong: tradeGood and dosFull[1].d refer to Poppy as 'his'.
audit.why: Poppy is female and the rest of the entry says 'her'.

notes: Left unasserted: whether Steadfast Presence's dash-stop interacts with Sanguine Pool. Riot's text says it stops enemy dashes; Sanguine Pool is described as sinking into a pool and becoming untargetable, not a dash, and the kit file gives it no dash flag — but the kits cannot settle whether Poppy's W blocks it in-game, so nothing was written either way. This is the same question the champion faces against every dash-stopper and would be worth confirming once at the champion level.
